8.text: Numerous reindeer are slaughtered to serve as provisions for the family

9.text: for the greater part of the summer. For this reason there is no need of

10.text: “substitute” sacrifices. A small fire, lighted by means of the fire-drill, is built

11.text: in front of the door, and an offering of marrow is burned in it.

12.text: Sacrifices of reindeer may take place on any unusual occasion; for

13.text: example, before beginning a journey (both going and coming), to ask the

14.text: protection of “spirits,” and at market-places to secure the good-will of the

16.text: When coming home after a long journey, the sledges are placed behind

17.text: the tent, a reindeer is slaughtered in sacrifice, and a fire is built, and “fed”

18.text: with fat, marrow, and blood-soup. A corral is built, and the reindeer used

19.text: on the journey are penned in it. The wife of the owner enters the corral

20.text: and paints each reindeer on its forehead and shoulders with soot mixed with

21.text: water, or with a decoction of alder-bark. This ceremony signifies the desire

22.text: to re-unite the reindeer and the family hearth.

28.text: In modern times this ceremonial, among the Reindeer Chukchee, is con-

29.text: nected with laying out the shed antlers on the ground. The breeding-males

30.text: lose their antlers immediately after the rut; the geldings, in the middle of

31.text: winter; the older ones, later; the young bucks, early in the spring; and the

32.text: does, after fawning, which happens as late as May with some of them.

33.text: All the antlers shed are picked up and kept for the ceremony, being

34.text: taken along when the people move from one pasture to another. When the

35.text: load becomes too heavy, a ceremonial is performed and the antlers are left

36.text: on the ground. The wealthy people consequently celebrate this ceremonial

37.text: three and even four times during the year; the poorer ones, only once or

38.text: twice. The spring is regarded as the proper time for the performance, since

39.text: most of the animals shed their antlers then.

42.text: boughs. Fire-drill boards are leaned against them, and the charms hung on
